claims.reason: The abstract explicitly states the authors propose a supervised machine learning model based on a range of linguistic features that classifies texts by difficulty level on a 5-point scale.
The cited text states that linguistic features explored for this task incorporate information from part-of-speech taggers and dependency parsers.
The cited text describes comparing different subgroups of features and mentions length-based, semantic, syntactic, and lexical features explicitly.
The cited text reports lexical features alone achieved about 0.8 F versus 0.81 F with the complete set, matching the claim.
The cited text states length-based, semantic and syntactic features in isolation showed similar or only slightly better performance than the baselines.
The cited conclusion states using only word-frequency features was almost as predictive as all features combined at the document level.
The abstract explicitly reports a 7% improvement in classification accuracy at the sentence level when combining features versus lexical features alone.
The cited conclusion states taking multiple linguistic dimensions into consideration is especially useful for sentence-level analysis.
